idiom_name: immutable record event + MediatR/MassTransit dispatch; System.Text.Json polymorphic serialisation
implementation_notes: A sealed record with positional parameters and init-only properties replaces the classic EventArgs-derived event class: it is immutable after construction and is the whole event contract. The publisher/subscriber structure is supplied by a dominant library rather than the BCL: MediatR routes a record implementing INotification to every INotificationHandler<T> in-process, MassTransit (or NServiceBus) publishes the same record as an integration event over a broker with consumer registration, retry and dead-letter handling. On the wire, System.Text.Json's [JsonPolymorphic]/[JsonDerivedType] attributes (or a JsonConverter before .NET 7) emit and resolve the $type discriminator, which is the built-in replacement for the hand-written type switch. The classic .NET event keyword plus EventHandler<TEventArgs> remains the right choice only for object-local notifications where the publisher is meant to know its listeners.
pitfalls: MediatR is in-process only: publishing before the transaction commits or expecting durability requires MassTransit/NServiceBus (or an outbox) instead.
Records give shallow immutability - a List<T> or array component can still be mutated by a handler, silently changing a fact other handlers see.
Polymorphic JSON needs the derived types opted in on the base type; an undeclared type throws at runtime, so the discriminator set must be kept in sync with the contract.
In-process handlers throwing can fail the publisher's operation; decide explicitly which notifications are fire-and-forget and which must gate the transaction.
